```plato
    // True when the hull has no area: fewer than three vertices, which is what
    // an empty, single-point, or collinear input produces.
    IsDegenerate(self: ConvexHull2D): Boolean
        => self.HullVertexCount < 3;
```

```plato
    // True when the hull encloses no volume: fewer than four vertices, which
    // is what an empty, degenerate, or coplanar input produces.
    IsDegenerate(self: ConvexHull3D): Boolean
        => self.HullVertexCount < 4;
```

```plato
    //==
    // # IPointSet2D / IPointSet3D
    //
    // No helpers are defined here: the defining points are an Array (IIndexable), so
    // the useful per-element conveniences already come from P2's generics on the
    // Points array — callers write `self.Points.IsEmpty`, `self.Points.First`,
    // `self.Points.Last`, `self.Points.Count`, `self.Points.At(i)`. Re-spelling any
    // of them at this layer would be pure rule-11 duplication. Aggregate reductions
    // (centroid, bounds) are the fold interface-gap noted at the top of the file.

    //==
    // # ILength
    //
    // Conveniences over a finite total Length. Half(Length) already comes from P1's
    // Half(IScalable); it is not respelled here.

    // True when the length is within `tolerance` of zero (a degenerate span).
    // Delegates to P1's AlmostZero(IReal, tolerance) rather than an exact == 0.0.
    IsDegenerate(self: ILength, tolerance: Number): Boolean
        => self.Length.AlmostZero(tolerance);
```
